To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a strong convolutional model is able to achieve competitive performance in person retrieval; (ii) part-level features are helpful for person retrieval, especially when they are refined by reassigning outliers to the parts to which they are most similar; (iii) our model is simple, easy to implement and can be trained end-to-end.

(i) we propose a strong convolutional network for person retrieval; (ii) we propose a novel RPP method for learning discriminative part-level features; (iii) our method outperforms the current state-of-the-art method on person retrieval.

1) Part-based convolutional baseline (PCB) is a strong baseline for person retrieval, which achieves competitive results compared to the state-of-the-arts; 2) Refined part pooling (RPF) method can be used as an effective post-processing method to improve the performance of PCB, and the improved method can further surpass the state-of-the arts.
